title: Organizations and Service Control Policies (SCPs)
hook: AWS Organizations groups accounts under one bill and governance model. Service Control Policies (SCPs) set maximum permissions — they cannot grant access, only deny it across member accounts.

blocks.text: AWS Organizations is a free service that manages multiple AWS accounts. Organizational Units (OUs) nest accounts (e.g., Workloads > Production). Service Control Policies (SCPs) attach to OUs or accounts and filter what IAM principals can do — even if an IAM policy allows an action, an SCP deny blocks it. SCPs do not affect the management account root user or service-linked roles in the same way — design guardrails knowing those exceptions.

entries.plainDefinition: A container for accounts within Organizations, often mirroring teams or environments.
entries.example: OU Production holds prod workload accounts.

entries.plainDefinition: Organization-level permission guardrail that sets the maximum permissions for accounts.
entries.example: Deny ec2:RunInstances except approved instance types.

entries.plainDefinition: Single payment method and volume discounts across all member accounts.

blocks.text: Enterprise AWS interviews expect you to explain SCPs as guardrails, not replacements for IAM. A developer IAM policy might allow s3:* but an SCP can deny s3:DeleteBucket on production OUs. SCPs are how security teams prevent region sprawl, unapproved instance types, or disabling CloudTrail.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: SCPs filter permissions downward — they never grant. IAM grants within the SCP ceiling.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Principal requests action
items.body: IAM user or role in member account calls an API.

items.title: IAM policy evaluated
items.body: Identity policy must allow the action.

items.title: SCP evaluated
items.body: Every attached SCP must allow — any explicit deny wins.

items.title: Resource policy (if any)
items.body: S3 bucket policy or KMS key policy may add another layer.

diagram.title: Organizations hierarchy
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  ROOT[Management account]
  ROOT --> SEC_OU[Security OU]
  ROOT --> WL_OU[Workloads OU]
  WL_OU --> PROD_OU[Production OU]
  WL_OU --> NONPROD_OU[Non-prod OU]
  PROD_OU --> ACC1[Prod app account]
  SCP_DENY[SCP: deny unapproved regions] -.-> PROD_OU

snippet.label: CLI: create OU and attach SCP
snippet.code:
aws organizations create-organizational-unit \
  --parent-id r-abcd \
  --name Production

aws organizations attach-policy \
  --policy-id p-FullAWSAccess \
  --target-id ou-abcd-12345678
snippet.explanation: OUs group accounts. Attach SCPs to OU — all child accounts inherit the guardrail.

snippet.label: CloudFormation: SCP deny leaving approved Regions
snippet.code:
Resources:
  RegionGuardrailScp:
    Type: AWS::Organizations::Policy
    Properties:
      Name: DenyUnapprovedRegions
      Type: SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY
      Content:
        Version: '2012-10-17'
        Statement:
          - Effect: Deny
            Action: '*'
            Resource: '*'
            Condition:
              StringNotEquals:
                aws:RequestedRegion:
                  - us-east-1
                  - eu-west-1
      TargetIds:
        - ou-abcd-12345678
snippet.explanation: SCP denies all actions outside approved Regions — applies to every principal in targeted OUs.

snippet.label: CLI: list effective policies for account
snippet.code:
aws organizations list-policies-for-target \
  --target-id 123456789012 \
  --filter SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY

aws organizations describe-effective-policy \
  --policy-type SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY \
  --target-id 123456789012
snippet.explanation: Debug 'access denied' by checking whether an SCP blocks the action before blaming IAM.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Using SCPs as the only permission mechanism — still need IAM least privilege. Attaching deny-all SCP without exception for break-glass roles. Forgetting SCPs do not grant — removing FullAWSAccess without replacing with allow statements locks accounts.

interviewTakeaways: Organizations groups accounts with consolidated billing and OU hierarchy.
SCPs set maximum permissions — deny filters apply even when IAM allows.
Debug access denied: check SCP before rewriting IAM policies.
60s: Org = multi-account governance. SCP = guardrail not grant. IAM works within SCP ceiling. Use OUs for prod vs non-prod policies.
Follow-up: what is the difference between SCP and permission boundary?
commonPitfalls: Saying SCPs grant permissions — that gets you rejected because SCPs only filter; IAM must still allow.
Strong answer: SCP is org ceiling; IAM is identity grant; both must allow for success.
Removing default FullAWSAccess SCP without understanding implicit deny impact.
Applying region-lock SCP without exception path for global services like IAM or CloudFront.

jsTsCorrelations.note: A Node CDK deploy to ap-south-1 fails with explicit deny when SCP locks Regions — the error looks like IAM but the fix is org policy, not role policy.
